learning_outcomes.text: By the end of the course, students should know the basic grammar and sufficient technical vocabulary to understand a wide variety of technical and academic texts in English.

They should also be able to understand the main ideas of complex texts related to their field of specialization, acquire knowledge on technical topics, answer questions, solve problems and express solutions both orally and in writing.
They should be able to give oral presentations on assigned topics.

Likewise, students are expected to be able to generally understand oral discourse to answer simple questions on technical topics, interact with their peers, and produce simple texts such as drafting a report on industrial accidents, writing letters requesting information, making outlines, and summaries.
In general, the stated objectives correspond to the B1 reference level established by the Common European Framework of Reference for Languages (2002).
Understanding and interpretation of texts and data, development of skills for their concretization and their clear and concise exposition.
Ability to transmit concepts, ideas, processes, etc., related to Industrial Engineering orally and in writing, clearly and correctly.
Ability for collaborative work and capacity for the development of multidisciplinary projects.
Ability to incorporate new knowledge in the field of Industrial Engineering, based on the acquired training and necessary for the evolution of technology.

syllabus_topics: Grammar: the future, relative clauses, comparative, articles, prepositions, passive voice.
teaching_methods: Reading a wide variety of technical texts in English
Individual work: written discourse production (drafting letters or technical reports, text summaries), Spanish to English translations, task and activity completion
Group work: information search and selection for oral presentations using PowerPoint
Active and dynamic methodology that promotes student participation and develops an autonomous attitude towards language learning and practice
Tutorials for resolving academic doubts or acquiring complementary information related to directed assignments

assessment_methods.method: Class attendance and participation in activities
Completion of individual written assignments (summaries and essays)

assessment_rules: The final grade is calculated based on: Final exam (50%), Class attendance and participation in activities (10%), Oral presentations and group work (20%), and Completion of individual written assignments (20%).
bibliography: Duna, M., D. Howey and A. Ilic, with N. Regan.2010. English for Mechanical Engineering in Higher Education Studies. Course Book. Reading: Garnet Education.
Philips, Terry. 2011. Technical English. Course Book. Reading: Garnet Education.
